chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Meets the Supervisory Heavenly Office's Blind Agent
chapter_meta_description: A sound he can't verify. A village too quiet. And a blind man who sees through invisibility by smell. Li Huowang's hunt for the Zuowandao takes a paranoid turn.
og_title: A Blind Man Detects Li Huowang's Invisibility—By Smell
og_description: In a village that feels too normal, a chance sound erodes Li Huowang's trust in his own senses. Then an old blind agent grabs him, claiming mud-devils hunt beneath the ground.
twitter_title: A Blind Man Smells Through Invisibility
twitter_description: A chance sound. A locked temple. A blind man who grabs Li Huowang mid-stride. The Zuowandao hunt gets eerie and quiet.

lore_anchors.definition: A government-backed bureau that manages rogue cultivators, supernatural disasters, and paranormal incidents in the Dao-Twisted World; agents carry rank tokens.
A fictional sect fusing Zoroastrianism and Nestorian Christianity; they worship the pain-feeding god Bashe and practice the horrors of the Thousand Greats Record.
The novel’s term for a type of earth-dwelling evil spirit; they move through mud and can only be caught one at a time.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How did Blind Chen detect Li Huowang’s invisibility?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He didn’t see him—he smelled the blood on Li Huowang. A brutally logical detection method grounded in the novel’s body-horror logic.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Blind Chen really who he claims to be?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The chapter deliberately leaves this ambiguous. His tone, his boast, and the lie Li Huowang tells back all suggest a mutual suspicion that will be resolved in later chapters.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Supervisory Heavenly Office?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a government supernatural-police bureau; its agents investigate rogue cultivators, evil spirits, and disasters. Rank is indicated by tokens (甲/乙/丙/丁 for high, 壬/癸 for low).
